claims.text: The target material is a quaternary equiatomic FCC random solid solution.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between phases.
Coherent-interface-mediated dislocation transfer makes yield strength insensitive to strain rate at sufficiently high temperature.
Thermal fluctuations overcome the activation barrier for dislocation glide at the temperature where rate insensitivity begins.
A stress-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation produces strong yield-strength strain-rate sensitivity because transformation nucleation and growth have a kinetic barrier.
Nano-precipitates, coherent interfaces, and stacking-fault networks influence dislocation mobility and phase-transformation nucleation.
At lower temperatures, dislocation glide is the primary deformation mechanism and yield strength is strain-rate sensitive because of thermally activated barriers.
At higher temperatures, coherent interfaces that permit dislocation transfer diminish strain-rate sensitivity.
CoNiCrFeMn nanowires deformed at 77 K can undergo an FCC-to-HCP transformation together with partial-dislocation activity, twinning, and stacking-fault formation.
Cryogenic FCC-to-HCP transformation keeps yield strength highly sensitive to strain rate.
Yield strength will exhibit a strain-rate-insensitive plateau above approximately 500 °C when interface-facilitated dislocation glide dominates.
At 77 K, yield strength will exhibit high strain-rate sensitivity.
Serrations or a distinct stress-strain plateau at 77 K are indicative of an FCC-to-HCP transformation and distinguish it from pure dislocation glide.
Standard CoCrFeMnNi alloys generally lose yield strength as temperature increases.
Standard CoCrFeMnNi alloys increase in yield strength with increasing strain rate because of dislocation drag.
The proposed behavior requires stacking-fault energy low enough for twinning or transformation but high enough to permit dislocation glide.
A high-stacking-fault-energy, purely single-phase alloy will not undergo the proposed transformation.
In-situ emergence of HCP diffraction peaks indicates phase transformation, whereas FCC peak broadening without HCP peaks indicates dislocation accumulation.
At 300 K, coherent interfaces should already reduce strain-rate sensitivity.

contradictions.description: The predicted rate-insensitive plateau is restricted to temperatures above approximately 500 °C, but the falsification rule assumes that coherent interfaces should reduce rate sensitivity at 300 K. Rate sensitivity at 300 K therefore would not directly contradict the stated high-temperature prediction.

The FCC-to-HCP mechanism is conditional on the alloy actually transforming. The combination of no detected HCP and no strain-rate sensitivity does not falsify that conditional claim; it instead indicates that its transformation antecedent was not met.
